review_boundary: The review covered the isolated Next.js 16.4 route/layout boundary, typed API adapter, browser session handling, entitlement fail-closed behavior, lock controls, allowlisted renderer metadata, shared SVG icon ownership and responsive shell CSS.
The supplied Pearson PTE Practice screenshots were used as the visual reference; no third-party source code or private website assets were copied.
Phase 05 session runtime, media capture, real progress results and live authenticated API smoke testing remain intentionally deferred and are not claimed by this gate.
No production deployment, external email delivery or persistent browser session was used as evidence.
review_basis: Student pages are grouped behind PracticeProvider and StudentShell; unauthenticated sessions redirect to sign-in and server data is never rendered as unlocked by default.

Catalog and entitlement responses are normalized through typed contracts; unknown renderer keys are reduced through the client allowlist and unavailable catalog data falls back to locked preview cards.
Locked buttons use native disabled semantics and do not navigate or issue session-start requests; exact UNLOCKED entitlement plus RUNNABLE catalog availability is required for an enabled action.
Inline SVG icons are owned by one AppIcon module and section icon selection is shared rather than repeated across route components.
Progress uses explicit empty markers instead of fabricated scores or response counts, while Home and Progress preserve the reference-shaped shell and skill surfaces.
